question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{3x+1} & ={2}^{x-1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3x+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x-1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x-1}).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+1 & =(x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+1 & =(x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ 3x+1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ 3x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-1 \\ x(3-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)) & =-(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+1) \\ x & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+1}{3-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$
